content.comment_body: Hello, I am working with a [product_name] 24CE [article_no]. I want to use a cursor button in my program. When I make a simple setup with a cursor key controlling Q1 output, I notice that after I release the button, Q1 output stays high for about 1 second—acting similarly to an OFF-DELAY. This issue does not occur with older [product_name] versions. What could be the reason?

This is a bug in [product_name] [version_no] and [product_name] [version_no]. If you migrate a program originally made with [product_name] prior to [version_no], this error can happen. The workaround is to first migrate the program using [product_name] [version_no], save it, then open and save it again in [product_name] [version_no]. If you do not have [product_name] [version_no], you can upload your program as a ZIP file and I can help with the migration.

Thanks for replying. I created a new program using [product_name] [version_no] on Windows 7 and tested it on a [product_name] [article_no], where everything works fine. I used counters and the program ran smoothly. However, with the [product_name] [article_no], it still doesn't function correctly. I am sending a sample program for reference.

analysis.insight_summary: Users describe a delay issue when using the cursor button in [product_name] [version_no]; the Q1 output remains active for about one second once the button is released, resembling an OFF-DELAY effect. This behavior is not present in older [product_name] hardware or earlier software versions. It appears tied to the combination of [product_name] [version_no] hardware and [product_name] [version_no] software, especially if programs are migrated from older software. Users expect output to change immediately, but the current hardware introduces a delay that affects usability.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the Q1 output to respond instantly when the cursor button is released, as experienced on older hardware and software versions. They want consistent real-time behavior across all [product_name] hardware and [product_name] software versions.
